firstWalk: You go further this time. Halfway, the lights move aside to let you pass, which is worse than if they'd blocked you. You turn back.
firstSketch: You sketch it again, from the same tussock. It's higher out of the water than last time; you draw the new course of stones.

afterBargainBroken.text: The landlord of the coaching inn sets a plate in front of you that you didn't order, pie and pickles and a slab of cheese. "On the house," he beams. "We like visitors here. Always have." The taproom door stands open on the green; swallows come and go under the eaves.

Nailed to the market cross is an old board of chalked tallies, harvests by year, in columns of seven. Every year is a good one. The chalk is fresh on all of them. Bees work the flowers in the trough below it.

The millrace is dry tonight, mud and stones, and the wheel is turning anyway, slow and steady and wet, as if water were running over it that you can't see. The evening is hot and still; the wheel's breeze is cool.

winterField: Tobias walks you up to the top field, where the farm meets the valley's land at an old drystone wall. On the far side the barley stands thick and gold. On the Fennick side it's thin, and patchy, and honest. "Seven good years down there," Tobias says. "Every year. Never up here." He puts his big hand flat on the wall. "Ma says the valley's luck is the valley's business."
